title: vscode-extension: `Export to React` emits an unused `import React`, so its output fails TS6133 under `noUnusedLocals`
body:
Found while removing the phantom `registerDefaultRenderers` import from the same
template (objectui#7837). Different defect class from that card — that one was a
symbol on no export of `@object-ui/components`, this one is a real import that is
never read — so it is filed rather than corrected in passing.

## The defect

`packages/vscode-extension/src/extension.ts` — `generateReactComponent()`, the body
of the **Export to React** command — opens every file it generates with:

```ts
import React from 'react';
```

The generated file's only JSX is a single SchemaRenderer element. (Spelled out in
words rather than written literally: GitHub deletes tag-shaped fragments from issue
bodies, fenced code blocks included.) Under the modern JSX transform —
`"jsx": "react-jsx"`, what Vite and Next give a new project today — the `React`
identifier is never referenced, so a consumer with `noUnusedLocals: true` fails to
compile the file the command just handed them.

## Measured, at objectui `bf51ca4ef`

Readings taken on the output the template actually produces — extracted from the
source on disk, then compiled against the built `dist/index.d.ts` of
`@object-ui/react` and `@object-ui/components`:

- `"jsx": "react-jsx"`, `strict: true` — clean, `tsc` exit 0.
- the same file, the same config plus `noUnusedLocals: true` — `tsc` exit 2:

```
Generated.final.tsx(1,1): error TS6133: 'React' is declared but its value is never read.
```

## Why nothing catches it

The same reason objectui#7837 survived: the preamble lives inside a **template
literal**, so this package's own `tsc --noEmit` sees a string, and no doc gate's
scan surface (`content/docs`, the per-app docs trees, `packages/NAME/README.md`,
the root `README.md`) reaches this file. objectui#7837 added a source-text pin on
the two lines it corrected; that pin does not and cannot judge this line.

## The correction is a decision, not a mechanical edit

1. **Drop the line.** Correct for `react-jsx`. Breaks anyone still on the classic
   `"jsx": "react"` transform, where the identifier is required at runtime.
2. **Keep it and make it used** — e.g. emit the component with an explicit
   `React.FC` annotation. Costs nothing at runtime and works under both transforms,
   but adds a type import the generated file otherwise does not need.

Option 1 is the obvious one, and it changes what the command emits for
classic-transform users — which is why this wants a decision rather than a drive-by
edit.

## Severity note

`packages/vscode-extension` is `private: true`: nothing publishes from it to npm, it
ships to the VS Code marketplace. Blast radius is the extension's own users, and
among them only those whose project turns `noUnusedLocals` (or the equivalent lint
rule) on as an error.
